authority.note: Derived join layer only; canonical model, registries, and per-qualification reports retain authority.

controls.description: Enterprise authorization resolves active memberships server-side, restricts governance changes to authorized roles, invalidates affected authorization/session state, audits changes, and refuses removal or demotion of the final active Owner.

Approval must come from a different currently eligible Owner/Admin with purpose-bound passkey step-up and exact action/target/revision binding; approval does not execute the action, and the initiator retry atomically consumes one continuation with replay refusal.

Typed policy candidates produce deterministic immutable revisions and manifests; activation proves loopback OPA observed revision/readiness before durable convergence, with known-good rollback/quarantine and explicit recovery proof when state is uncertain.

Temporary exceptions are restricted to catalog.install and exact app/device/human/policy revision, reject wildcard/global scope, expire within at most 60 minutes and can be revoked; matching enforces active unexpired exact scope.

WebAuthn ceremonies bind short-lived server-owned challenges to purpose, origin and RP ID; passkey assertions update signer counters and purpose-bound step-up expires independently of the browser session.

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Sanitized configuration booleans and startup reason codes only.
scenarios.purpose: Production/default-off state never enables harness, destructive, Owner, or test-bypass authority implicitly.

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Sanitized binding booleans, profile name, target scope, and lifecycle classification.
scenarios.purpose: Synthetic assurance authority is purpose-bound, target-bound, runtime-bound, non-Owner, and non-destructive.
scenarios.title: Synthetic Ed25519 session and capability boundary

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Status codes, bounded response metadata, marker-presence booleans, and route classifications.
scenarios.purpose: Proxy-visible headers never become harness authority and harness routes remain direct-loopback only.
scenarios.title: Caddy never forwards qualification proof into FastAPI authority

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Boolean readiness checks, status codes, and sanitized failure classes.
scenarios.purpose: Runtime readiness is based on API, message-bus, and worker truth rather than PM2 online alone.
scenarios.title: API health/readiness and PM2 readiness distinction

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Fixed subject/handler booleans and sanitized bus health only.
scenarios.purpose: Browser clients cannot choose NATS subjects or commands; worker execution remains on the registered subject and domain handler.
scenarios.title: Assurance execution remains FastAPI to NATS to worker owned

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Canary count, leak count, redaction booleans, and sanitization markers.
scenarios.purpose: Secret-like values, credentials, private-key material, cookies, and NATS credential shapes never survive normalized persistence.
scenarios.title: Assurance evidence contains only normalized sanitized output

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Registered tool results, normalized findings, bounded evidence references, baseline delta, and resource metrics.
scenarios.purpose: Scanner work remains worker-owned, sequential/resource-bounded, excludes user media, and produces normalized sanitized findings/evidence.
scenarios.title: Existing Security projection and scanner lifecycle are available

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Ready/degraded status, loopback/browser exposure booleans, and sanitized reason code.
scenarios.purpose: Policy admission remains loopback-only, browser-hidden, revision-aware, and fail-closed when not ready.
scenarios.title: OPA loopback readiness and policy revision consistency

scenarios.normalized_evidence: File/byte counts, match counts, fixed marker booleans, and no source excerpts.
scenarios.purpose: Frontend contains no direct NATS or shell execution surface and checked backend/Caddy evidence boundaries remain present.
scenarios.title: Canonical source preserves browser, shell, NATS, and user-media boundaries

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Probe ID, fixed method/path identity, status code, rejection boolean, bounded response metadata, and duration.
scenarios.purpose: Every fixed malformed/forged request is rejected without creating authority or intentional persistent mutation.
scenarios.title: Fixed malformed authentication and input probes remain denied

scenarios.normalized_evidence: Registry hashes, canonical IDs, execution defaults, retry policy, and coverage lists.
scenarios.purpose: Every current AP path is classified by registered assurance coverage and every reference resolves to canonical source.
scenarios.title: Current canonical threat model is complete and executable statuses are explicit

scenarios.normalized_evidence: AP ID/name, classification, reason, STRIDE/OWASP mapping, controls, and human-review flag.
scenarios.purpose: No current AP path is silently treated as tested; coverage limitations remain explicit.
scenarios.title: Every current AP path has a bounded execution classification

adversarial.purpose: Qualification-only reviewed adversarial checks limited to fixed local control-boundary requests.

deep.purpose: Manual-only extended assurance profile; approved heavyweight tools execute through the fixed DEV-PC lanes and the existing worker-owned Security path.

smoke.purpose: Fast bounded runtime assurance using existing low-power Security and critical control-boundary checks.

standard.purpose: Normal runtime qualification with the existing Quick scanner, API boundary probes, policy readiness, and threat coverage.

truth_boundaries.coverage: Evidence coverage ratio; never a security score.
truth_boundaries.human_review: Human-governed review remains separate from automated checks and cannot be auto-promoted to PASS.
truth_boundaries.partial: Valid evidence exists but coverage or resulting condition is incomplete.
truth_boundaries.pass: The registered invariant held for the observed qualification evidence; not proof it can never fail.
truth_boundaries.qualification: Bounded evidence for one exact qualification and runtime SHA; not a universal security claim.
truth_boundaries.scenario: Registered invariant and safe execution definition; not a scanner product.
truth_boundaries.threat_model: Saved modeled threats and controls; not live monitoring.
